call_points.text: Net debt ₹234 Cr at June 2026; gross debt ₹1,960 Cr including ₹934 Cr of lease rental discounting, cash ₹1,727 Cr.
₹1,500–1,800 Cr of commercial capex remains, fully tied up; construction finance converts to lease rental discounting on completion.
Pre-leasing pipeline in excess of 3 million sq ft under discussion across the two under-construction commercial projects.
Elevated employee and marketing costs reflect launches this quarter versus none a year ago; costs to track launches through the year.
Residential sales volumes moderated through the quarter on global uncertainty, tightening liquidity and cautious consumer sentiment.
Management refrained from giving explicit FY27 pre-sales guidance due to evolving macroeconomic conditions.
The company continues to target adding approximately 2 million sq ft of residential and 1 million sq ft of commercial space annually.
Residential market in Delhi NCR has seen moderation and caution over the last 6 months amidst global uncertainties.

penalties.details: Notice received for Max Estates Gurgaon Two Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company) under Section 122 of Haryana Municipal Corporation Act, 1991 read with Haryana Municipal Corporation Advertisement Bye-Laws, 2022 imposing penalty of ₹5,64,399/- for displaying advertisement, in contravention of Section 122 of Haryana Municipal Corporation Act, 1991

penalties.details: Order under Section 271FAA imposing penalty of Rs 50,000 for inaccurate/incomplete filing of Statement of Financial Transaction (Form 61A) for FY 2024-25 in the case of Max Estates Gurgaon Two Limited (wholly owned subsidiary of the Company)
penalties.impact: Financial impact limited to penalty of Rs 50,000; no impact on operations. Given the small quantum, the impact is not material at the consolidated level. The Subsidiary will file the appeal to Commissioner of Income-Tax (Appeals) as the error is due to technical glitch on tax Portal

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Pharmax Corporation Limited, a subsidiary of Max Estates Limited, received a Show Cause Notice in Form GST DRC-01 dated July 27, 2026, under Section 73 of the CGST/DGST Acts for FY 2022-23, proposing demand of Rs 5.90 Crores (including tax, interest and penalty), relating to alleged excess / ineligible input tax credit. The matter was at the show cause notice stage, with no final demand or order passed.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Department of Trade and Taxes, Government of NCT of Delhi (Office of the Assistant Commissioner / GSTO)
tax_litigation.status: The Company has opposed the proposed demand, considering it factually incorrect and without merit, as the major amounts of Input Tax Credit (ITC) identified by the Department had already been reversed in the Company's books and GST returns. The proposed demand appears to have arisen from an automated reconciliation of vendors' outward supplies, GSTR-2B and GSTR-9 disclosures, without considering the ITC reversals already undertaken by the Company. The matter is currently pending adjudication. The reply to the Show Cause Notice has been submitted, and the date of personal hearing is awaited.
